Been thinking a lot on the revenue problem after @Atko's latest announcement. I know first hand how hard it is to run a site or business while strictly and stubbornly holding onto your ideals. But I think there is a way to do this that wont compromise them or introduce the issues we've seen on other sites, like Reddit.

When thinking of "Ads done right", the first thing that comes to mind is Penny Arcade. They struggled to stay afloat as well and tried a few different approaches, like donations. They weren't happy with that solution, but really didn't want to go ad happy as this was when ads were really ramping up their shitty behavior. The compromise was transparency and communication with their users and white listing ads that they felt their users would genuinely be interested in. They didn't just let an ad company go hog wild on their site. They personally approved each and every ad to make sure their users would be interested and that they weren't too intrusive to the site.

I think Voat can do something similar, but it needs to go farther. One of the biggest concerns with "selling out" or doing ad systems is the community's legitimate fear of losing control. We don't want to go down the path were advertisers start demanding a ban on the more unpleasant subs with the threat of pulling their revenue entirely.

So I think the best solution is to allow each sub to decide on it's own if it wants to allow ads and get to white list the ads individually or by category. /v/movies, /v/fitness, /v/loseit, /v/gaming, etc all have rather obvious ad categories they would lean towards. And making it mod controlled allows the mods and community to feel like they are still in control and not the admins or a 3rd party.

There would still need to be admin overrides and controls though. Ad companies should also be able to request to be removed from certain subs. Instead of demanding a sub be banned they can just be banned from that sub. The mods wouldn't see their ads in their list anymore.

The down sides I see to this are: 1) The ad companies do still have some power. If Voat becomes too dependent on the revenue stream then they could still make demands backed by threats, even though there are tools to remove them from places they don't like. 2) This is not a small amount of code effort. It's rather large and so no value would be seen for some time. 3) This is a lot of overhead to manage the approval process for both the ad companies and the Voat communities. That could be a full time job in itself.

But I think this is the closest we can get to have low intrusive revenue while still maintaining a majority of the control.

Constitution

  1. Vision

  2. Owner
    1. AskVoat is to be owned by system. There will be no (other) Level 1 moderators.

      1. This moderator will have no vote in the Governing Council, and will conform to the responsibilities of the Owner as outlined here.

      1. The new Owner can come from within or outside of the Governing Council.

  3. Governing Council
    1. Decisions concerning AskVoat will be made by a Governing Council, comprised of all and only the Level 2 moderators of AskVoat.
      1. Level 2 moderators added without the approval of the Governing Council, are not themselves members of the Governing Council.
    2. Each member of the Governing Council will have a single equal vote on each motion.
      1. Each member will vote to support the motion, reject the motion, or abstain.
      2. Members who abstain will be removed from the pool for purpose of determining whether the motion has achieved the necessary majority.
    3. Motions requiring a simple majority that end in a tie, will be put to a community referendum.
      1. The poll will remain open for at least 24 hours, and will have a finite timeframe.
  4. Rights and Duties of the Owner
    1. The Owner will exercise actions for AskVoat at the request of the Governing Council.
      1. The Owner will not perform any administrative action in AskVoat without the agreement of the Governing Council, except where that action is explicitly provisioned within the Constitution.
      2. The Owner will not perform any administrative action explicitly forbidden by the Constitution.
      3. The Governing Council will not ask the Owner to perform actions that they can successfully perform without the intervention of the Owner.
    2. The Owner will not set Anonymized Mode to active.

  5. Rights and Duties of the Governing Council
    1. Members of the Governing Council have the right to remove posts and comments that breach the rules, without need to consult other members of the Governing Council.
    2. A member of the Governing Council may tender their resignation at any time.
    3. Any motion not explicitly covered in the Constitution will be decided by simple majority.
      1. The Constitution may be amended only with unanimous agreement of the Governing Council.
      2. A member of the Governing Council may be stood down only with the unanimous agreement of all other members of the Governing Council.
      3. A new member of the Governing Council may be elected only with a two-thirds majority (≥).
      4. The Rules and Suggestions may be amended only with a two-thirds majority (≥).
    4. The Governing Council, by simple majority, may declare to allow the Owner to make a decision.
      1. The Owner must turn down this offer unless there is a state of emergency.
  6. Emergency Provision
    1. In the event of an emergency, where a reasonable attempt has been made to reach the Governing Council, and has failed to gather a quorum, the Owner may institute any and all actions not explicitly forbidden in the constitution.
      1. These actions will remain in effect until a quorum can be gathered, and the Governing Council has voted on what action is desirable.
